questions.q: What is the key difference the lesson draws between a procedure and a workflow?
options: A procedure answers what one person does for one task; a workflow answers what happens as a request moves across different roles
There is no real difference between a procedure and a workflow
A workflow only applies to IT systems, while a procedure applies to policy
A procedure is always longer and more detailed than a workflow
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes single-person step-by-step instructions (procedure) from a multi-role, end-to-end path (workflow).

questions.q: Which of these is one of the six shared stages of a governance workflow?
options: Triage / classification
Marketing approval
Vendor contract renewal
Annual budget planning
questions.explain: The six stages are intake, triage, routing, resolution, verification, and closure — triage is one of them.

questions.q: In the policy exception request workflow example, why does the lesson say the request needs an expiration date?
options: So the exception doesn't quietly become permanent policy
Because all governance documents legally expire after 90 days
Expiration dates are only needed for access request workflows, not exceptions
To automatically notify the sponsor every time it expires
questions.explain: An expiration date keeps a time-bound exception from silently turning into an unreviewed, permanent change to the standard.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about choosing a ticketing system or data catalog tool for running governance workflows?
options: The tool is a delivery mechanism, not the design — the stages and accountability should be designed first
The tool must always be selected before any workflow stages are designed
Only large organizations are allowed to use ticketing tools
Workflows cannot be run through spreadsheets under any circumstances
questions.explain: The lesson warns that a well-configured tool running an undefined process just produces fast, untracked chaos — design comes first.

questions.q: In the access request workflow example, who typically approves the request before IT provisions access?
options: The data owner (sometimes through a steward first)
Any employee in the company, with no approval needed
Only the executive sponsor personally
The requester approves their own request
questions.explain: The lesson describes the access request routing to the data owner for approval, sometimes via a steward, before IT provisions access.
